title: KCP event envelope (DESIGN.md §11.3): identity, ordering, typing, actor/causation, classification, payload
description: Event envelope per §11.3, field-for-field: event_id, installation_id, realm_id, project_id?, stream_id, stream_sequence, project_sequence?, type, schema_ref, resource_ref, resource_revision?, actor_ref, causation_ref?, correlation_ref, occurred_at, classification_ref, payload_digest, payload | payload_ref, ext?. Exactly one of payload/payload_ref is present (the § renders them as an alternation). stream_sequence is dense and monotonic within one aggregate stream; project_sequence is dense and monotonic for all Kovee-owned events in one project. Event type names are reverse-domain names ending in a major version (e.g. dev.kovee.space.contribution-appended.v1); the dev.kovee.* namespace is reserved for system-generated events, and namespace registration — like payload retention by classification — is enforced by the service, not this shape. payload_digest is a §11.8 typed digest whose type is fixed by this schema field; DESIGN.md does not pin which of the two §11.8 constructions covers event payloads — a recorded K0 gap (spec/schemas/README.md).

payload.description: Inline event payload validated by the schema at schema_ref; registered application event payloads are capped at 64 KiB (§11.8), enforced at admission. Any JSON value here; each payload schema closes it.

payload_ref.description: Durable reference to an externalized payload; access is authorized at read time (§11.4).

ext.description: Extensions keyed by a reverse-domain namespace (§11.9); never identity, authorization, budget, or policy.

identifier.description: Opaque identifier, at most 128 bytes (§11.8); visible-ASCII alphabet is a K0 extraction decision (spec/schemas/README.md).

safeNonNegativeInteger.description: I-JSON safe integer (§11.8 rejects unsafe integers).

eventType.description: Reverse-domain event type name ending in a major version, e.g. dev.kovee.space.contribution-appended.v1 (§11.3). A breaking payload change uses a new major event type (§11.9). Major versions start at 1 (the § shows only .v1 and never a .v0) — recorded extraction decision.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 date-time. DESIGN.md does not pin the encoding of occurred_at; RFC 3339 follows I-JSON's (RFC 7493 §4.3) date-time recommendation — recorded extraction decision.

digestHex.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 value of a §11.8 typed digest. The digest type/domain is fixed by the schema field holding it; a bare 32-byte value cannot be substituted across digest fields (§11.8).
